prompt: A car wash's revenue fell 15% last year. The number of cars washed was flat. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Revenue has likely fallen while the number of cars held steady.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: A rival opening nearby has likely cost the car wash customers.
options.feedback: The number of cars washed was flat, so the customers are still coming.

options.text: Customers are probably picking the basic wash over premium.
options.feedback: Right. Flat volume with falling revenue means revenue per car fell, and a shift to cheaper washes is a likely, testable cause. I'd check the mix of wash types over time.

options.text: Something about how the business makes money has probably changed.
options.feedback: Too vague to test: what changed, and what data would show it?

explanation: The data shows cars washed flat and revenue down 15%, so revenue per car fell. Likely cause: customers are picking the basic wash over premium. To test it, check the mix of wash types over time. If the mix is unchanged, look at discounts or memberships.
